h1:
Kalasin 2 Days 1 Night
Dinosaur Country–Lam Pao Dam–Old Town
intro: Kalasin is an Isan province that fits a two-day, one-night break just right. Day one goes all in on dinosaurs at the Sirindhorn Museum and the Phu Kum Khao excavation pit, then rolls on to Lam Pao Dam for an evening sunset. Day two loops into the old town of Fa Daet Song Yang, pays respects at Phra That Yakhu, and heads home. This is a plan with the timings, routes and a budget you can actually count on — just follow it.

blocks.html: Kalasin sits in the upper Isan region, about an hour and a half from Khon Kaen and roughly two hours from Udon Thani. Most people come as a side trip from Khon Kaen, or fly into Udon and rent a car from there. The main sights are spread out a fair way from the town centre, especially Sahatsakhan district, which puts the dinosaur museum and Lam Pao Dam close together. Having your own car or a rental is by far the easiest way to get around. The old town of Fa Daet Song Yang is over in Kamalasai district, in a different direction, so we've slotted it into day two to catch on the way back.

blocks.title: Plan before you set off
blocks.html: The Sirindhorn Museum is closed every Monday. If your trip lands on a Monday, flip the order — do the dam and old town first, and save the museum for a non-Monday so you don't miss it.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Dinosaur country + an evening by Lam Pao Dam

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Sahatsakhan: dinosaurs in the morning, Lam Pao Dam at dusk

items.activity: Leave central Kalasin and head for Sahatsakhan district
items.note: It's about 28 km, roughly 30–40 minutes. Grab breakfast in town first if you like — the rice-soup and congee spots around Phirom Road open early.

items.activity: Enter the Sirindhorn Museum (Phu Kum Khao Dinosaur Research Centre)
items.note: Thailand's first dinosaur museum, open 09:00–17:00, closed Mondays. Adult entry is a small fee of a few tens of baht, with discounts or free entry for kids and seniors. Plan on about 1.5–2 hours to see the exhibits properly.

items.activity: Walk up to the Phu Kum Khao excavation pit and see real dinosaur bones in the rock layers
items.note: The dig is behind the museum, on the hill at Wat Sakkawan. This is where the Phuwiangosaurus sirindhornae fossils were found — you can see bones still embedded in the rock where they were unearthed. Wear comfortable walking shoes.

items.activity: Lunch on Isan food around Sahatsakhan, or eat on the way to the dam
items.note: Along the road to the dam there are several waterside garden restaurants, such as Suan Ahan Klin Lamduan. Order grilled fish, som tam and laab for a relaxed midday meal.

items.activity: Rest / check in near Lam Pao Dam or in town
items.note: The afternoon sun is harsh — take a breather to recharge before heading out for the cool evening air.

items.activity: Head to Lam Pao Dam, walk the dam crest and swim at Dok Ked Beach
items.note: Dok Ked Beach is open 07:00–19:00, free entry, free parking, with umbrellas, mats and tubes for rent. It's a freshwater beach where Kalasin locals come to hang out.

items.activity: Catch the sunset from Thepsuda Bridge
items.note: The longest freshwater bridge in Thailand, about 30 km from the dam crest. The evening light on the water is gorgeous. If you're short on time, watch the sunset from Dok Ked Beach instead — it's closer.

items.activity: Dinner by the dam — grilled prawns, grilled fish, jaew hon
items.note: The waterside restaurants near the dam serve fish straight from Lam Pao. Salt-grilled fish with a hot pot of jaew hon broth is a meal that suits the setting perfectly.

blocks.html: Day one keeps the driving short and avoids doubling back — the museum, the excavation pit and the dam all sit in the Sahatsakhan–Yang Talat zone, which links up neatly. If you're travelling with kids, the dinosaur museum and Dok Ked Beach are the two spots they'll love most.

blocks.title: Book the activities in your Kalasin trip ahead
blocks.text: Booking online ahead on Klook or GetYourGuide is usually cheaper than the gate and skips the queue. Pick only the experiences you actually want — prices and availability are shown live on each site.

items.label: Day trips from Kalasin
items.note: Out and back in a day

blocks.text: Day 2 — Fa Daet Song Yang old town + souvenirs before heading home

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Kamalasai: Phra That Yakhu–ancient town–Praewa silk

items.activity: Breakfast in town, pack up and check out
items.note: Try khao jee, sticky rice with grilled pork skewers, or Isan-style congee in central Kalasin before you set off.

items.activity: Drive to the ancient town of Fa Daet Song Yang, Kamalasai district
items.note: About 19 km from the town centre, roughly 25 minutes. It's a moat-and-earthwork town from the Dvaravati period.

items.activity: Pay respects at Phra That Yakhu, the great stupa in the rice fields
items.note: The largest stupa in Fa Daet Song Yang, with an octagonal base — an ancient monument that's a landmark for the town. Dvaravati-era sandstone boundary markers (sema) are scattered across the area. It photographs beautifully in the morning before the sun gets harsh.

items.activity: Stop at a temple in Kalasin town on the way back
items.note: Wat Klang, a royal temple, is an old temple central to the province. Drop in for a quick blessing before you go souvenir shopping.

items.activity: Souvenirs: Praewa silk and local snacks
items.note: Praewa silk from Ban Phon, Kham Muang district, is Kalasin's famous textile. If you can't make it all the way to Ban Phon, you can find it in souvenir shops in town — leave time to browse.

items.activity: A final lunch to close the trip — Isan food in town
items.note: Som tam and laab spots in town, like those around Pradit Road, have plenty to choose from. Order som tam pla ra, laab and koi to round things off before the drive back.
About 1.5 hours back to Khon Kaen or 2 hours to Udon Thani. Leave time for a fuel stop and a break along the way.

items: 1 night's accommodation — a hotel or resort in town or by the dam, around ฿500–1,200 per room (split between two, that's ฿250–600 each)
Sirindhorn Museum entry — a few tens of baht per person, with discounts or free entry for kids and seniors. Dok Ked Beach and the dam are free
Food — ฿80–200 per meal, around ฿500–800 for the whole trip
Fuel / car rental — a sedan rental runs about ฿900–1,300 per day plus fuel, averaged out and split within your group
Budget total — around ฿1,200–1,800 per person if you go as a group of 2–4 and split the car

blocks.html: Kalasin has no airport or train station in town. The popular option is to fly into Udon Thani or Khon Kaen and rent a car from there. Khon Kaen is closer — about an hour and a half along Highway 209. There are also coaches from Bangkok (Mo Chit) to Kalasin bus terminal, taking roughly 8–9 hours. In town there are songthaews and motorcycle taxis, but the sights are spread out beyond the town, so having your own vehicle is by far the most convenient.

blocks.title: Best time to go
blocks.html: The cool season (November–February) is comfortable and the best time for the dam and the old town. In the rainy season Lam Pao Dam fills up and looks lovely, but the beach may close at times. In the hot season the sun is fierce, so plan outdoor activities for the morning and evening.

blocks.text: Food you shouldn't miss on the trip

items.name: Grilled Lam Pao Dam fish
items.blurb: Fresh fish from the dam, salt-grilled and eaten with a punchy jaew dip — a must-order when you're by the water.

items.name: Jaew hon
items.blurb: An Isan hot pot in a herbal broth, with beef and vegetables to dip. Several spots in town keep it as a signature dish.

items.name: Som tam–laab–koi
items.blurb: The Isan staples, done with bold flavour at Kalasin's spots. The Pradit Road area has plenty to choose from.

blocks.html: If you want to dig deeper into the food — the Lam Pao fish restaurants, the jaew hon spots and the cafés in town — we've got a separate guide linked below to help you lock in the meals across these two days more tightly.

faq.q: Is 2 days and 1 night enough for Kalasin?
faq.a: It's enough for the main sights — the Sirindhorn Museum, the Phu Kum Khao excavation pit, Lam Pao Dam, Dok Ked Beach, and the old town of Fa Daet Song Yang with Phra That Yakhu. If you want to add Thepsuda Bridge at a relaxed pace, or go all the way to Ban Phon to buy Praewa silk, bump it up to 3 days and 2 nights.

faq.q: What days is the Sirindhorn Museum open and how much is entry?
faq.a: It's open daily 09:00–17:00 except Mondays, when it's closed. Adult entry is a few tens of baht, with discounts or free entry for children, seniors and monks. Allow about 1.5–2 hours to walk through, including the excavation pit.

faq.q: Is there an entry fee for Lam Pao Dam and Dok Ked Beach?
faq.a: Lam Pao Dam and Dok Ked Beach are free to enter, with free parking. Dok Ked Beach is open 07:00–19:00 and has umbrellas, mats and tubes for rent. Your only costs are food at the waterside restaurants and extras like a raft cruise.

faq.q: Can you visit Kalasin without your own car?
faq.a: You can, but it's harder, because the sights are spread out beyond the town. In town there are songthaews and motorcycle taxis. We'd suggest renting a car from Khon Kaen or Udon Thani and driving yourself, or hiring a van with a driver for the day — either makes it much easier to keep to this plan's timings.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Kalasin?
faq.a: The cool season, November to February, is best — cool weather and comfortable for walking the dam and the old town. In the rainy season the dam fills up and looks lovely, but the beach may close at times. The hot season is still doable, but avoid the midday sun by scheduling outdoor activities for the morning and evening.
